title: Deterministic computation separated from LLM verbalization
old_model: A single LLM prompt would calculate the chart, choose rules and produce a reading in one opaque step.
observed_limitations: Calculation errors and interpretation disagreements would be difficult to distinguish.
The same input could produce different underlying reasoning depending on model wording.
Source provenance and deterministic regression would be weak.
current_model: Deterministic programs own calculable chart facts and canonical rule execution; symbolic/graph procedures handle explicit relations; LLMs assist with explanation and verbalization but do not own rule truth or probability truth.
rationale: Separate deterministic facts, source-grounded inference and natural-language presentation so each can be audited with the appropriate method.
consequences: Chart and canonical facts need deterministic tests.
LLM-generated additions require provenance and unsupported additions must be blocked.
A fluent explanation is not evidence that a rule is canonical.
what_remains_valid: LLM may still assist with source extraction, candidate generation, explanation and language organization under review.
Human Gate and source-span verification remain necessary for semantic promotions.
boundaries: This is a project architecture boundary, not a claim that traditional sources used modern AI terminology.
This record does not certify every Product runtime path as complete.
